question: Who was known as the father of civil services in British India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Charles Cornwallis**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Charles Cornwallis is **known as the "Father of Civil Services in India**" because he reformed and modernized the civil service during the British Raj.
 
• **Warren Hastings** is credited with laying the foundation for the civil service
 
• ** Cornwallis's contributions to the civil service**: 
 
 
• Divisions: He** introduced two divisions **of the civil service: 
 
• Covenanted: **Only Europeans held higher government positions **
 
• Uncovenanted: Indians could enter the lower levels of administration 
 
• Modernization: He modernized and rationalized the civil service 
 
 
 
• The c**urrent civil services of India are based on the pattern of the former Indian Civil Service of British India**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Warren Hastings (1773-1785)**

 
 
• He was the** first Governor-General of India.**
 
• He is **known for establishing the Dual System**, which divided the administration of Bengal between the Company and the Nawab.
 
• He **also introduced judicial reforms** by establishing the Supreme Court at Calcutta.
 
 
 
• **Lord Wellesley (1798-1805**)
 
 
• He was a **Governor-General with an aggressive expansionist policy.**
 
• He** introduced the Subsidiary Alliance System,** which required Indian rulers to accept British protection in exchange for military support.
 
• This **led to the annexation of several Indian states and the Third Anglo-Maratha War.**
 
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856)**
 
 
• He was another **Governor-General who expanded British territory in India.**
 
• He **introduced the Doctrine of Lapse,** which allowed the British to annex Indian states if their rulers died without a natural heir.
 
• He **also initiated the construction of railways and telegraph lines**, which improved communication and transportation but also contributed to the unification of India under British rule.
